六级大纲词汇 · 19英文原文

The Worker by the Well

水井旁的女工 · 594 词 · 6 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A town planned to commemorate a workers' uprising with a stone naming local patriots. It could be a milestone for families who had long kept silent. Sora, a young historian, found that the list left out a mill worker who had helped emancipate families held in debt. A tribune in the old union had denounced the owners, while a regimental order let soldiers repress the revolt. The woman's letters condemned the atrocious conditions in the mills. The official account had described the trade in lofty terms and omitted the suffering beneath its prosperity. She also opposed the uprising's more ruthless leaders. Sora asked why the committee treated those positions as contradictory.

2Its chair said the woman had given water to soldiers who besieged the town. Some union leaders had called her a foe. A witness described the well differently. Women and children could not leave their houses under a suppressive curfew. The worker took a bucket across the line and asked both sides to let people through. She acted after a boy collapsed. Sora wanted the stone to record that act. A knight in the king's guard had left an account of the afternoon. In it he addressed the ruler as "Your Majesty." Even he remembered who had kept the well open.

3A committee member reacted with indignation. He said an account of kindness could perpetuate the old habit of excusing oppression. Sora showed him the next page. The worker deplored the punishment a foreman had inflicted on an apprentice. Subordination to the owners left workers dependent on a single employer. Even their children were subordinate to the same system. She opposed vengeance against apprentices' families. Their suffering was already a harsh consequence of the owners' greed. The member remained indignant about putting an opponent of the union beside its leaders. He agreed to mediate if Sora could authenticate the letters.

4The conservator found that the woman had used a nickname in one letter and her full name in another. A retired clerk recognized the salutation and a reference to a well behind a chapel. A photograph from the period showed a woman in a plain cloak carrying a bucket near it. Sora did not claim that the image proved her identity. She used an independent payroll entry to match the names. The comparison clarified a line about an old superstition. Some people had believed the well was cursed.

5The committee accepted the match but disagreed about the label. One draft described the woman as a martyr, although she had survived the fighting. Another praised her as an icon of patriotism. Sora said the two labels could stifle discussion about the actual work. The local archive displayed the letter beside a list of the families who gained their liberty. Their names gave the act of emancipation a human scale. At the ceremony the chair could inaugurate the exhibit by reading the exact passage about the well. A short reading was more apt than a tribute to the town's former prestige or a display of patriotic zeal.

6A child traced her name when the crowd had dispersed. He asked if she had worn armor. Sora showed him the photograph without making him guess who it pictured. She read the line in which a woman had put her bucket down so a boy could drink first. He looked back at the other names, then pointed to the well at the end of the lane. He wanted to see how far she had carried it. Sora knew where to start if he asked for the story again.

六级大纲词汇 · 19中文译文

水井旁的女工

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1镇上打算立一块石碑纪念工人起义，把当地爱国者的名字刻上去。对长期保持沉默的家庭而言，这可能是个重要时刻。年轻历史学者索拉发现，名单漏掉了一位帮助负债家庭获得自由的女工。老工会的一名代言人曾公开谴责厂主，军队则奉命压制反抗。女工在信里痛斥厂里恶劣的条件。官方记载只赞颂这个行业，略去了繁荣背后的苦难。女工同时反对起义中那些过于狠厉的领袖。索拉问，委员会为什么觉得这两种立场互相矛盾。

2委员会主席说，女工曾给围困镇子的士兵送水，因此有工会领袖把她当成敌人。一名证人对水井旁的事有另一种说法。严厉的宵禁让妇女和孩子无法出门。一个男孩倒下后，女工提着水桶越过分界线，请双方放居民通过。索拉想把这一行动记在石碑上。国王卫队的一名骑士也记过那个下午，还在报告里用“陛下”称呼君主。连他也记得是谁让大家还能到井边打水。

3一位委员很气愤。他说，把这件事讲成一次善举，可能延续替压迫开脱的老习惯。索拉给他看了下一页。女工痛斥工头对学徒施加的处罚。工人受制于一个雇主，连孩子也被绑在同样的制度里。女工反对向学徒的家人报复，因为厂主的贪婪已经让他们吃了太多苦。委员仍对把一名反对过工会的人和工会领袖刻在一起感到不满，但答应只要索拉能证实信件是真的，就出面调解。

4文物保护人员发现，女工在一封信里用了绰号，在另一封信里用了全名。退休职员认出信的开头，也认出小教堂后面那口井的描述。当年的一张照片拍到一个披着素色斗篷的女子，提着水桶走过那里。索拉并不把照片当成身份证明，而是找了一份独立的工资名册核对名字。对照也说明了信中关于一个旧迷信的话。过去有人以为那口井受了诅咒。

5委员会接受了身份核对的结果，却没谈拢说明牌怎么写。有人称她为烈士，可她在战斗中活了下来。另一个版本把她奉为爱国象征。索拉说，这两种称号都可能让人忽略她究竟做了什么。当地档案馆把信和获得自由的家庭名单放在一起。那些名字让人看见，所谓解放具体落到了哪些人身上。揭幕时，主席可以直接朗读写水井的那一段。比起长篇称颂小镇旧日的声望，或表达满腔爱国热情，简短的原文更合适。

6人群散去后，一个孩子沿着刻出的名字比画，问她当年穿没穿盔甲。索拉给他看了那张照片，也没让他猜照片里的人是谁。她念出那句话，一位女子放下水桶，让男孩先喝。孩子回头看了看周围那些名字，又指向小巷尽头的水井。他想知道，她提着桶走了多远。如果他再问这个故事，索拉知道该从哪里讲起。
